segments.text: In the beginning, God made the heavens and the earth. Day by day, He filled the world with light, sky, land, seas, plants, stars, animals, and people.
Creation Week invites kids to slow down and notice God’s good world with wonder, gratitude, and joy.
Every flower, ocean, animal, and star points back to God’s care. Children can learn to thank Him for the beautiful things they see each day.
The story ends with rest, showing that God’s work was good. It gives kids a gentle rhythm for wonder, work, worship, and peace.

The Israelites stood at the edge of the sea with danger behind them and no road ahead. God told Moses to lift his staff, and the water opened into a dry path.
Kids will see that God can make a way when things feel impossible and that trusting Him can move us forward.
Step by step, the people crossed safely. This story reminds kids that faith can begin with one small step on the path God opens.
When they reached the other side, the people sang and celebrated. They remembered that God had rescued them with mighty love.

Daniel kept praying to God even when it became dangerous. When he was thrown into the lions’ den, God protected him through the night.
This story shows kids that faith can stay strong in hard places, and that God is near when we choose what is right.
Daniel did not have to be loud to be brave. His quiet trust teaches children that prayer can give courage even when everyone else is afraid.
When morning came, Daniel was safe. The king saw that Daniel’s God was powerful, faithful, and worthy of praise.

David was a young shepherd who trusted God with his whole heart. When the giant Goliath frightened the army, David remembered how God had helped him protect his sheep before.
With a sling, five smooth stones, and brave faith, David stepped forward. This story reminds kids that courage grows when we remember God is with us.
David did not need heavy armor to do what was right. Children can learn that a faithful heart, a listening spirit, and trust in God are stronger than fear.
When the battle was over, everyone saw that the victory belonged to God. David’s story helps kids remember that small hands can do brave things with God’s help.

Esther became queen at a time when her people needed help. With wisdom and courage, she spoke up even though it was scary.
Her story reminds kids that God can place us right where we are needed, and bravery can begin with one honest choice.
Esther listened, waited, and chose the right moment to speak. Kids can learn that courage and wisdom often work together.
Because Esther cared for others, her brave choice helped save many lives. Her story makes kindness feel strong.

Jonah tried to run away from what God asked him to do. A storm, a great fish, and three quiet days helped Jonah learn that God’s mercy is bigger than fear.
This story helps kids talk about second chances, listening to God, and choosing kindness even when it is hard.
Jonah learned that God cares for people we may not understand. Children can see that mercy is wide, patient, and full of hope.
By the end, Jonah had to learn that God’s love reaches farther than his own plans. That lesson is still good for every heart.

Joseph belonged to a large family. His father, Jacob, gave him a special colorful coat. Joseph also had dreams that surprised his brothers. Instead of sharing his happiness, his brothers grew jealous.

Their jealousy led them to make a terrible choice. They took Joseph away from home and sold him to travelers going to Egypt. Joseph lost his coat and the comfort of his family, but God did not leave him.

Life in Egypt was difficult. Joseph worked faithfully, even when others treated him unfairly. Over time, God helped him understand dreams. When the ruler of Egypt needed help, Joseph explained that years of plenty would be followed by years when food was scarce.
Joseph helped store grain so people would have food later. When the hungry years arrived, his brothers came to Egypt for grain. They did not recognize the brother they had hurt so long ago.

At last, Joseph told them who he was. He cried, welcomed them, and helped his family. Their wrong choice was still wrong, but Joseph chose forgiveness instead of revenge. His story reminds us to notice jealousy, ask for help, and choose kindness. God can bring hope even after a painful beginning.

Moses learned that God can use ordinary people for brave work. From the burning bush to leading God’s people, Moses had to trust God one step at a time.
Kids will follow Moses as he listens, obeys, and discovers that God gives courage for the journey.
Moses did not always feel ready, but God stayed with him. This helps children see that they can ask for help and still take the next brave step.
Through each challenge, Moses learned to listen for God’s voice. His story reminds kids that leadership starts with obedience.

Noah loved God and listened carefully, even when the job seemed too big. God told Noah to build an ark because a great flood was coming, and Noah obeyed one step at a time.
This story helps kids see that obedience matters. Noah trusted God, cared for his family, and welcomed the animals safely into the ark.
After the rain, God placed a rainbow in the sky as a promise. Kids can remember that God keeps His word and watches over every family that trusts Him.
At the end, Noah and his family stepped into a fresh new world. They praised God together and began again with thankful hearts.

Naomi had lost people she loved and was returning to Bethlehem. Her daughter-in-law Ruth could have stayed in her own country, Moab. Instead, Ruth chose to stay beside Naomi and share her journey.
Ruth promised to make Naomi’s people her people and to trust Naomi’s God. Together, they reached Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest. They needed food, so Ruth looked for a way to help.

She went into the fields to gather grain that the harvesters left behind. This was called gleaning. Ruth bent down, picked up the grain, and kept working. Little handfuls slowly became enough to take home.

The field belonged to Boaz, a relative of Naomi’s family. He heard about Ruth’s faithful care. Boaz made sure she could work safely, offered water and food, and asked the workers to leave extra grain for her.

That evening, Ruth brought grain and leftover food back to Naomi. Naomi was encouraged by the kindness they had received. Ruth continued gathering through the harvest. Her love was more than a promise: it became patient, useful work. We can care for our families through small helpful actions, and welcome people who are starting again in a new place.

Joshua led God’s people toward Jericho, a city with strong walls and tightly closed gates. The people could not simply walk through. God gave Joshua instructions that required trust, patience, and careful listening.

For six days, the people marched around the city once each day. Priests carried the ark of the covenant, a reminder of God’s presence, and seven priests carried trumpets. The people waited quietly for Joshua’s signal.

Each day, they returned to camp. They had followed the instructions, but the walls were still standing. Waiting can feel difficult when we want something to happen right away. The people kept taking the next faithful step.
On the seventh day, they marched around Jericho seven times. Then the trumpets sounded and Joshua gave the signal. The people shouted, and the walls fell. God had opened the way as he had promised.

Rahab and her family were brought to safety, just as the spies had promised when she helped them. This story reminds us that trust includes listening and keeping our promises. We can practice patience, work together, and ask God for courage while we wait. One obedient step can prepare us for the next.
